lines.text: Tobin's letter reached me the night before the Tourney. Nine pages this time, mostly drawings, spelled like a man who had learned his letters last spring. Which he had.
Bram's letter came in the same packet. Bram's letters were always exactly one page. This one was one line.
All well. Do not worry. Bram.
Tobin's letter explained what all well meant.
Saltmouth had a harbour, a lighthouse, and nobody to guard them. So Bram marched twenty fishermen up from the coast, and taught them to fight.
Shields up! Spears level! You there. That is not how you hold a spear.
It's how you hold a gaff, Steward. Works on a cod.
They fought like men landing fish, with nets and hooks. Bram said it was a disgrace. It also worked. They netted Tobin twice.
Then there were the wolves.
Rook, Birk and Tarn were half grown now, each as big as a wolf. And Bram had decided they would be soldiers.
Sit. Sit. Rook, sit. Birk, stop herding the fishermen. Tarn. Tarn, wake up.
Tobin drew Tarn asleep on top of Bram. He drew it three times. I think it was his favourite page.
But by the second week, Rook could run a message to Saltmouth and back in half a day. And nothing got past Birk on the ridge.
The beacons were Bram's idea too.
A horse takes a day to reach Saltmouth. A light takes a heartbeat. If anything comes for us, I want to know before it arrives.
Tobin built towers on the hilltops, all the way to the coast, each with a rimeglass heart and iron shutters, so the light could blink.
Candles on hills. In my day, we used a boy with a loud voice.
On the first test night, every tower blinked in turn, all the way to the sea. And the lighthouse at Saltmouth blinked back.
Then the drawings stopped.
Three riders on the east ridge, Steward. No banners. They did not hunt. They counted.
Tarn found where they had camped, and brought back a glove. Fine southern leather, burnt orange, with gold thread at the cuff.
Orange and gold. Penhallow.
At the bottom of the last page, in Tobin's worst spelling, was one more line.
Bram says not to tell you about the riders on the ridge. So I am not telling you.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eighty-five, coming soon.
